> 讼。有孚，窒惕，中吉，終凶。

Here is a character almost every commentary reads as a picture, and almost every commentary is wrong about the structure.

## 讼 is 從言，公聲

說文: 讼，爭也。從言，公聲.

It is a phonetic compound. 公 is the sound, not the meaning.

Which matters because the pleasing reading is "speaking (言) in the public hall (公)" — an appealing picture, and not what the character is.

That is the most common kind of easy slip in 易 commentary: a reading that is smooth loses to a reading that is correct.

The original sense is simple: contention. Its institutional form is argument in a public court over who is right and who is wrong. Not a private quarrel — a public dispute.

## 窒 is blocked

說文: 窒，塞也.

有孚窒惕: there is trust, there is substance, and the way through is blocked, and so it is stifled.

This is the most painful sentence in the hexagram, and it is not "he had no case."

It is: he had the case, and could not get the words through.

## 惕 is the attitude that remains

窒 is the situation. 惕 — vigilance, fear — is what the person still has to do about it.

The situation is blocked, so the person holds himself alert. Nothing else in the hexagram is available to him at that point. Which is a very exact description of being in the right and unheard.

## 逋 is withdrawal, not flight

說文: 逋，亡也 — to flee, to get away.

But 不克訟，歸而逋 is not "he ran." It is: he could not win the case, so he withdrew himself from the contest.

The 象 adds 復即命 — he returned to what he was charged with. Withdrawal here is not defeat; it is ending participation.

## 眚 is the misfortune you caused

說文: 眚，目病也。從目，生聲 — the original sense is an eye disease, a film growing over the eye; thence misfortune, fault.

The extension is what matters: 眚 is specifically disaster brought on by one's own fault, distinguished from 災, which is disaster from outside.

So 無眚 is not "no trouble happened." It is "there is no account here that he opened himself."

## 鞶帶 and 褫

鞶帶 is the waistband of a nobleman's ceremonial dress — a grant from the ruler.

褫 is 奪衣, to strip the garment, to take back the honor.

終朝三褫之: one morning, stripped three times.

Which is the hexagram's verdict on winning by litigation: the reward arrives and is removed repeatedly, inside the same day.

## 作事謀始

The 象's instruction: in the beginning of a matter, lay out the boundaries.

Note what it is not. It is not "make a plan." The object of 謀始 is very specific: 界 — the boundary.

A dispute is not caused by disagreement. It is caused by a boundary that was never drawn, and which each side then drew privately.

## Why 中吉終凶

The judgement line is a schedule: good if stopped in the middle, bad if carried to the end.

So the hexagram is not against speaking. It is against continuing — the point at which contention stops being a way to find the boundary and becomes a way to win.

That point is not at the start, and it is not detectable from inside by intensity. It is detectable by whether a boundary is being established or a person is being defeated.

## A test

Take a disagreement you are in. Ask whether the thing you are actually seeking is a line on the ground or a verdict. If it is a verdict, you are already past 中.
